messages:
viv: quick sync re: lease / adapter boundaries across hosted/dedicated/private — we need a concise contract for leases, eviction signalling, and what stays warm vs. purge on evict.
raj: Yeah. Runtime team keeps hitting ambiguity between "soft" vs "hard" evict. Soft = let existing streams finish, don't accept new requests. Hard = immediate cut. We should name them.
beth: Proposal: three results: ACCEPT, DRAIN, FORCE. ACCEPT = normal renew. DRAIN = runtime stops new sessions, continues in-flight up to drain_timeout. FORCE = immediate stop.
viv: love the explicit names. defaults? I'd suggest: hosted: drain_timeout=90s, dedicated: drain_timeout=30s, private: drain_timeout=300s (customer preference).
raj: Also need a canonical way to tell SDKs about the state. Suggest HTTP header + final stream event. Header: `X-RW-Lease-State: ACCEPT|DRAIN|FORCE` + `X-RW-Lease-Reason`. For streaming, final event: `{"type":"lease_update","state":"DRAIN","reason":"PREEMPT"}`.
beth: Important: differentiate control-plane-initiated evictions vs runtime-initiated (OOM/restart). Add origin field: controlplane|runtime|ops.
infra-bot: deploy: canary rollout of lease-protocol v1 scheduled 2026-03-24T02:00Z.
raj: Cache semantics: if eviction origin=AUTHZ or COMPROMISE -> MUST invalidate tenant caches immediately. If origin=PREEMPT then invalidate optional (best-effort) unless tenant marked for hot-reattach.
viv: to make that operable, runtime should include `cache_action` in the event: `invalidate|preserve|async_invalidate`. Also expose `POST /internal/cache/invalidate` for operators.
beth: note on async_invalidate: runtime should emit `cache_invalidate_job_id` and `GET /internal/cache/job/{id}` for status; control plane can poll.
raj: token semantics: claim tokens must include `mode` (hosted/dedicated/private), `resource_pin` (model:id@sha), and `capabilities` array. No wildcard model pins. Example JWT payload: `{"sub":"rt-1","mode":"dedicated","pin":"m-bert@sha256:abcd","cap":["kvcache","batching_v2"],"exp":4848488599}`.
viv: for private mode allow `claim_delegated:true` and `issuer` field that can be customer url (we'll validate signature chain).
beth: metrics & alerting: emit `lease_renew_success{mode}`, `lease_renew_fail{reason}`, `lease_forced_evictions_total{reason,region}`. Add SLO for renew latency <100ms p90.
ops: ops-playbook: on mass DRAIN/FORCE events, slow down control-plane renew rate (circuit-breaker) and enable emergency routing to cold-fallback model. Add runbook link: https://redwood.internal/playbooks/lease-surge.
raj: eviction priority: prefer evicting low-weight tenants first. Weight = billing_tier * (1 + ephemeral_penalty). Provide override tag `evict_priority` per-tenant.
viv: implementation note: avoid cache stampede during reattach. Suggest randomized reattach jitter + leaky-bucket reattach window. Document in RFC.
beth: edge-case: private runtimes behind customer NAT — control plane can't push events. Runtime must write local journal `/var/log/redwood/lease-journal` and mark last-seen claim. On reconnection, it POSTs journal to control plane endpoint.
infra-bot: alert: previous test showed 10% of private runtimes behind firewall did not receive invalidate for PREEMPT, logged in QA ticket #4321.
ops: final ask: RFC should include default numbers, wire examples, CLI commands (`rwctl lease inspect --runtime RT-ID`), and a rollback plan.
viv: I'll draft RFC with these conventions and defaults: hosted(drain=90s,grace=120s), dedicated(drain=30s,grace=60s), private(drain=300s,grace=600s). Tagging @raj @beth @ops for review.
raj: I'll review + add test cases for SDK behaviour on DRAIN->FORCE transitions.
beth: I'll add cache backpressure handling and API shapes.
viv: Thanks all, will open PR soon. :rocket:
